subtitle: Stone Crowns Unraised, Power Still Remembered

panels.shot: epic wide of Halebidu temple complex under a moody sky, low-angle showing flat roof where towers should rise
panels.action: Veera Ballala II and Queen Umadevi stand on the jagati of the Halebidu twin temple, surrounded by carved walls and silent shikharas that never rose, the capital stretching beyond them.

dialogue.text: In Veera Ballala II’s proud age, Halebidu’s twin temple blazed with sculpture yet waited for its missing towers—an unfinished crown that still holds his and Queen Umadevi’s power in stone.

i18n.hi: वीर बल्लाल द्वितीय के गौरवमय समय में हलेबीड़ु का जुड़वां मंदिर मूर्तियों से जगमगाया, पर अपने गायब शिखरों का इंतज़ार करता रहा—अधूरी मुकुट, जिसमें उसकी और रानी उमादेवी की शक्ति पत्थर में कैद है।

panels.shot: slow push-in from aerial view of Karnataka hills towards Dorasamudra-Halebidu
panels.action: A serene landscape of hills, lakes, and fields in southern Karnataka leads the eye toward the dense cluster of Dorasamudra-Halebidu, its stone temples catching the sun.

dialogue.text: In the late twelfth century, between the hills of Karnataka, Dorasamudra—later called Halebidu—grew from a quiet town into the glittering heart of Hoysala power.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के अंत में, कर्नाटक की पहाड़ियों के बीच दोरसमुद्र—जो बाद में हलेबीड़ु कहलाया—एक शांत कस्बे से होयसल साम्राज्य के चमकते दिल में बदल गया।

panels.shot: regal medium-wide inside a palace hall, Ballala II seated, Umadevi beside, court gathered
panels.action: Veera Ballala II sits on a carved throne, youthful yet firm, Queen Umadevi at his side, ministers and generals arrayed before them under a high timbered roof.

dialogue.text: Veera Ballala II inherited a realm of rising strength. From Dorasamudra he looked north and south, ruling with Queen Umadevi, as campaigns and culture advanced together.

i18n.hi: वीर बल्लाल द्वितीय को उभरती ताकत का राज्य मिला। दोरसमुद्र से वह उत्तर–दक्षिण देखता, रानी उमादेवी संग राज करता, जहाँ युद्ध और संस्कृति साथ–साथ बढ़ते रहे।

panels.shot: dynamic montage wide showing army on one side, temple worksites on the other
panels.action: On one half of the frame Ballala II rides at the head of armored cavalry leaving the city; on the other half, stone blocks and chisels move around the foundations of an elaborate temple.

dialogue.text: As Ballala rode out to test his strength against neighbours, masons and sculptors worked steadily at home. Power was measured in land and armies—and in stone rising from the earth.

i18n.hi: जब बल्लाल पड़ोसियों से अपनी ताकत परखने घोड़े पर निकला, घर पर राजमिस्त्री और मूर्तिकार लगातार काम में लगे रहे। ताकत ज़मीन और फ़ौज से मापी जाती थी—और धरती से उठते पत्थर से भी।

panels.shot: architectural low-angle close-up on Hoysalesvara temple base and friezes
panels.action: The camera lingers on the dark stone jagati of the Hoysalesvara temple, layered with friezes of elephants, horses, and warriors marching endlessly in silent, precise rows.

dialogue.text: On the lake’s edge at Dorasamudra, the great Hoysalesvara–Shantalesvara complex rose—the jagati wide as a royal court, its walls filling with belts of elephants, horses and battle scenes carved in detail.

i18n.hi: दोरसमुद्र की झील किनारे होयसलेश्वर–शांतलेश्वर का विराट समूह उठा—जगती राजदरबार जितनी चौड़ी, दीवारें पट्टियों में भरती हुईं: हाथी, घोड़े और लड़ाइयों के दृश्य बारीक नक़्क़ाशी में।

panels.shot: close-up of an inscription panel being carved by an artisan
panels.action: An artisan crouches by a smooth stone slab, hammer and chisel poised, carefully incising rounded Kannada letters into the surface beside the temple wall.

dialogue.text: Around 1121 CE onward, inscriptions recorded gifts and names: donors who paid for walls, images, offerings. Their letters still cling to the stone, long after voices fell silent.

i18n.hi: लगभग 1121 ई. से शिलालेखों में दान और नाम दर्ज होने लगे: वे दाता जो दीवारों, मूर्तियों, नेवैद्यों का खर्च उठाते थे। आवाज़ें थम गईं, पर उनके अक्षर आज भी पत्थर से चिपके हैं।

panels.shot: busy courtyard scene with merchants supervising delivery of stone blocks
panels.action: In the temple courtyard, richly dressed merchants oversee the unloading of stone blocks from ox-carts, gesturing toward the sculptors as workers strain at ropes and wheels.

dialogue.text: Inscription lines speak of Ketamalla, Kesarasetti and others. These merchants did not stand in the shadow of kings—they stepped into the record as patrons, their wealth turning to carved walls.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख की पंक्तियाँ केतामल्ला, केसारसेट्टी और कई नामों की बात करती हैं। ये व्यापारी राजाओं की छाया में नहीं खड़े रहे—वे खुद बतौर संरक्षक दर्ज हुए, उनकी दौलत पत्थर की दीवारों में बदल गई।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of a sculptor carving a deity, merchant watching respectfully
panels.action: A sculptor, bare-backed and focused, chips fine details into a deity’s crown while a merchant patron stands nearby with folded hands, watching the form emerge from rough stone.

dialogue.text: For each image—a god’s face, a dancing figure, a battle scene—someone paid, someone chose. The Hoysalesvara did not grow by royal will alone. It was a ledger of many hands and hopes.

i18n.hi: हर मूर्ति के लिए—देव का चेहरा, नाचती आकृति, युद्ध का दृश्य—किसी ने भुगतान किया, किसी ने चुनाव। होयसलेश्वर सिर्फ राजआदेश से नहीं बढ़ा। यह अनगिनत हाथों और उम्मीदों की बहीखाता था।

panels.shot: medium shot in palace with Umadevi receiving reports while Ballala is away
panels.action: Inside a quiet hall, Queen Umadevi sits with palm-leaf records and priests before her, listening intently, while a royal sword and armor lie unused on a stand, hinting at Ballala’s absence on campaign.

dialogue.text: When Ballala II went to war, records credit Umadevi with authority. While armies moved, she heard petitions, watched accounts and kept temple and town turning in his absence.

i18n.hi: जब बल्लाल द्वितीय युद्ध पर निकला, लेखों में उमादेवी को अधिकार मिलता है। फ़ौजें चलती रहीं, पर वह फरियाद सुनती, हिसाब देखती और उसके रहते मंदिर–नगर का चक्र चलता रहा।

panels.shot: thoughtful medium-two shot on palace balcony overlooking Halebidu temple site
panels.action: On a stone balcony, Umadevi stands at the railing, Ballala II beside her, both gazing toward the twin temple where walls are richly carved but the roofline is still flat and open.

dialogue.speaker: veera_ballala_ii_and_umadevi
dialogue.text: “The walls sing already. One day, towers will rise above them.”

i18n.hi: “दीवारें तो अभी ही गा रही हैं। एक दिन, इनके ऊपर शिखर उठेंगे।”

panels.shot: transition wide shot moving from Halebidu to Shravanabelagola hill
panels.action: The view shifts from the Halebidu temple to the distant stone hill of Shravanabelagola, its Jain monuments gleaming, as if connected by an invisible thread of patronage and road.

dialogue.text: The Hoysalas’ reach was not only Shaiva. In 1182, at Shravanabelagola, an inscription in Akkana Basadi named Ballala II’s support for Jain monks and their quiet, white-stone shrines.

i18n.hi: होयसलों की पहुँच सिर्फ शैव मत तक नहीं थी। 1182 में, श्रवणबेलगोला में, अक्कन बसदी के शिलालेख ने बल्लाल द्वितीय की जैन भिक्षुओं और उनके शांत, सफेद–पत्थर मंदिरों को दी गई मदद दर्ज की।

panels.shot: serene medium-wide inside Akkana Basadi with Jain image and inscription stone
panels.action: Within Akkana Basadi, a Jain image sits in calm pose as a stone slab covered in neatly carved Kannada letters stands upright nearby, light slanting across its surface.

dialogue.text: That carved text at Akkana Basadi reveals a plural court. In the same reign that filled Halebidu with Shaiva sculpture, Jain basadis received land, lamps and food from the same royal hand.

i18n.hi: अक्कन बसदी का वह खोदा हुआ लेख एक बहुल दरबार दिखाता है। जिस राज में हलेबीड़ु शैव मूर्तियों से भरता रहा, उसी में जैन बसदियों को ज़मीन, दीप और अन्न वही राजहाथ देता रहा।

panels.shot: juxtaposed medium shot, Ballala in Jain shrine, Umadevi near Shaiva temple
panels.action: Ballala II is shown respectfully entering a Jain shrine at Shravanabelagola, while in a mirrored frame Queen Umadevi stands near a Shaiva temple doorway, priests at both places blessing them.

dialogue.text: Ballala II’s age braided many paths. Jain monks, Shaiva priests, merchant donors and queens shared a web of power and patronage. Stone keeps their names together where words might divide them.

i18n.hi: बल्लाल द्वितीय का समय कई राहों को गूंथता है। जैन साधु, शैव पुरोहित, व्यापारी दाता और रानियाँ—सबने सत्ता और संरक्षण का जाल बाँटा। जहाँ शब्द बाँट सकते थे, पत्थर उनके नाम साथ रखता है।

panels.shot: architectural high-angle over Halebidu temple plan showing two shrines, open roofline
panels.action: A high, plan-like view of the Hoysalesvara–Shantalesvara complex shows the twin shrine layout, detailed walls and richly carved outer faces, but the top remains a flat roof without soaring towers.

dialogue.text: Architects like Gerard Foekema later walked this plan and traced its lines. They found a near-complete temple in ground and wall—but no great superstructures. The shikharas never rose.

i18n.hi: आर्किटेक्ट जेरार्ड फूक्मा जैसे लोग बाद में इस योजना पर चले और इसकी रेखाएँ पढ़ीं। उन्हें ज़मीन और दीवारों में लगभग पूरा मंदिर मिला—पर बड़े ऊपरी ढाँचे नहीं। शिखर कभी उठे ही नहीं।

panels.shot: contemplative low-angle from roofline looking up at empty sky
panels.action: From the temple roof, the view looks upward where tower bases end abruptly, meeting only open sky, as birds wheel above the silent stone.

dialogue.text: Later generations asked why. Was work halted, plans changed, or destruction at play? The record stays quiet. In the absence of clear words, scholars refuse easy, single answers.

i18n.hi: बाद की पीढ़ियों ने पूछा क्यों। काम रुका, योजना बदली या विनाश हुआ? रिकॉर्ड ख़ामोश है। साफ़ शब्दों के बगैर विद्वान आसान, एकमात्र जवाब से बचते हैं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of Halebidu temple through changing light and passing centuries
panels.action: The temple sits unchanged as the light shifts from dawn to dusk, then to cloudy skies and modern visitors, hinting at centuries passing while its roof remains low and intricate carvings endure.

dialogue.text: UNESCO’s 2023 eye notes the missing towers as a loss of integrity, yet still calls Halebidu’s sculpture outstanding. An unfinished crown did not erase the value of what stands.

i18n.hi: यूनेस्को की 2023 की नज़र अधूरे शिखरों को अखंडता की कमी मानती है, पर हलेबीड़ु की मूर्तिकला को अब भी अद्वितीय कहती है। अधूरी मुकुट ने खड़े हुए हिस्से की कीमत नहीं मिटाई।

panels.shot: poetic medium shot of Ballala and Umadevi as ghostly presences among temple visitors
panels.action: Modern visitors walk the jagati, while faint, translucent figures of Ballala II and Umadevi seem to stand among them, looking down at the stone stories they once helped set in motion.

dialogue.text: Ballala II’s campaigns faded, Umadevi’s decisions passed into silence. Yet each passerby at Halebidu reads their age in stone, through friezes funded by merchants and shrines blessed by many faiths.

i18n.hi: बल्लाल द्वितीय की मुहिमें धुंधली पड़ गईं, उमादेवी के फ़ैसले ख़ामोशी में खो गए। पर हलेबीड़ु से गुज़रता हर इंसान उनके युग को पत्थर में पढ़ता है—व्यापारियों की चंदा से बने फ्रीज़ और कई मतों से धन्य मंदिरों में।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of a single intricate sculpture panel on the Halebidu wall
panels.action: A close view captures a single lively panel: warriors, dancers, animals, and a god carved with dizzying precision, every ornament crisp despite the centuries.

dialogue.text: This temple’s story is not about a missing peak alone. It is about work shared, lines of credit and trust, a queen’s steady hand and a king’s broad patronage, all frozen into basalt.

i18n.hi: इस मंदिर की कथा सिर्फ एक गायब शिखर की नहीं। यह बाँटे गए काम, भरोसे–उधार की लकीरों, रानी के स्थिर हाथ और राजा की व्यापक संरक्षण–शक्ति की कहानी है, जो बेसॉल्ट में जम गई है।

panels.shot: final wide sunset shot of Halebidu temple silhouette, flat roof against glowing sky
panels.action: At sunset, the Halebidu temple stands in silhouette, its roofline flat but strong against the glowing sky, carvings catching the last light as shadows pool around the base.

dialogue.text: Halebidu waits for towers that may never come, yet the work completed has become a masterpiece. It reminds us that history’s greatness often lies in what was done, not in what was perfectly finished.

i18n.hi: हलेबीड़ु उन शिखरों की प्रतीक्षा करता है जो शायद कभी न आएँ, पर जो काम पूरा हुआ वही कृति बन गया। यह याद दिलाता है कि इतिहास की महानता अक्सर किए गए काम में होती है, न कि पूरी तरह मुकम्मल समाप्‍तियों में।

title_i18n.hi: हलेबीड़ु अपने शिखरों की राह देखता है

subtitle_i18n.en: Stone Crowns Unraised, Power Still Remembered
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर के ताज अधूरे, ताकत अब भी ज़िंदा
